--- title: "UK E-Commerce Transactions: Part 1 - Data Cleansing Pipeline" description: "Resolving missing customer IDs, system cancellation anomalies, and non-product line items across 540k retail transactions." author: "Fab" date: "2026-09-09" categories: [Python, pandas, Data Cleansing, Data Visualization, E-Commerce] format: html: code-fold: show code-summary: "Click to toggle code" toc: true toc-depth: 3 --- ## Project Goal Build a data cleansing pipeline in Python for the **UK Online Retail dataset** (541,909 raw records), resulting in a reliable dataset that can be used for customer behaviour, revenue analysis and further explorations ### **Key Results & Business Impact** * **Data Quality Restoration:** Discarded **150,000+ noisy rows** (~27.8% of the raw dataset), resolving 135k null `CustomerID` records and non-product fees (`AMAZONFEE`, `POSTAGE`). * **Storage Optimization:** Converted raw CSV data into compressed **Apache Parquet**, reducing file footprint from **~48 MB to ~10 MB** (80% compression). --- ## Data Pipeline Implementation Load the necessary libraries to work with the dataset. The parquet dataset was created by importing the dataset locally, converting to parquet (using *df.to_parquet()*) and the final cleaned Parquet dataset created by the Python pipeline below. ### Step 1: Import the required libraries and checks ::: {#1efab9bb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd import sys from pathlib import Path # Make sure the post dir is on Python's path sys.path.append(str(Path(".").resolve())) #file_path = sys.path.append(str(Path(".").resolve())) ``` ::: ::: {#8da685f9 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Load cleaned Parquet dataset online_retail = pd.read_parquet("../data_dcp/OnlineRetail.parquet") #online_retail['InvoiceDate'] = pd.to_datetime(online_retail['InvoiceDate']) online_retail.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=46} ```{=html}

Summarise the data in tabular format: ::: {#e2f51798 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import GT, style, loc # import the cleaned dataset cleaned_retail = pd.read_parquet("../data_dcp/clean_online_retail.parquet") audit_data =[ { "Metric": "Total Rows", "Raw State": f"{len(online_retail):,}", "Cleaned State": f"{len(cleaned_retail):,}", "Impact": f"-{len(online_retail) - len(cleaned_retail):,} rows removed" }, { "Metric": "Unique Stock Codes", "Raw State": f"{online_retail['StockCode'].nunique():,}", "Cleaned State": f"{cleaned_retail['StockCode'].nunique():,}", "Impact": "Non-inventory stock codes removed (POST, D, etc.)" }, { "Metric": "Cancelled Invoices ('C')", "Raw State": f"{online_retail['InvoiceNo'].str.startswith('C', na=False).sum():,}", "Cleaned State": f"{cleaned_retail['InvoiceNo'].str.startswith('C', na=False).sum():,}", "Impact": "Isolated to prevent negative revenue distortion" }, { "Metric": "Zero / Negative Unit Prices", "Raw State": f"{(online_retail['UnitPrice'] <= 0).sum():,}", "Cleaned State": f"{(cleaned_retail['UnitPrice'] <= 0).sum():,}", "Impact": "Price anomalies and bad entries removed" } ] # Create dataframe so output renders nicely df_audit = pd.DataFrame(audit_data) # Pass to GT for executive-level Quarto rendering ( GT(df_audit) .tab_header( title="Data Quality Audit Pipeline", subtitle="Before vs. After Impact Analysis — Online Retail II" ) .cols_label( Metric="Audit Metric", **{"Raw State": "Raw Data", "Cleaned State": "Cleaned Data"} ) .tab_style( style=style.text(weight="bold"), locations=loc.column_labels() ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=55} ```{=html}
